files.role: Crate module facade and asynchronous footer-only exact file-version recognition.
ranges: SPDX; public concat,datatypes,format,reader,testing,version,versions,writer modules; io is pub(crate), compatibility_tests private cfg(test). Public LanceEncodingsIo reexport exposes selected IO type despite module visibility. Schema conversion, IO adapter, exact dispatch, writer facade and type checker are now covered; V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 concrete writers and shared structural pipeline are covered separately. The V2_0 writer, testing helpers, exact-version compatibility tests and fixture generator sources are also covered. Full reader IO, writer_tests.rs, V1 writer and individual binary fixtures remain pending.

Imports shared MAGIC, core errors, ObjectStore/Path and exact version. determine_file_version(store,path,known_size)->Result<ConcreteFileVersion> obtains size via await store.size only if unknown, checked-converts it to usize or InvalidInput with path. Supplied usize size is trusted without checking actual length; no explicit size lookup then. Underlying open behavior is delegated, so this does not prove all HEAD requests avoided.

Reject size<8 with InvalidInput source text and path, then await open_with_size and exactly requested range size-8..size. Compare footer[4..] to MAGIC; mismatch returns contextual InvalidInput. No explicit received-length check: fewer than4 returned bytes can panic on slice; other non8 lengths fail magic comparison. Store/range IO errors propagate. No full file parse or schema/page integrity check.

Decode first two little-endian u16 values from four bytes, then delegate ConcreteFileVersion::from_footer_numbers. Magic match implies exactly8 returned bytes for this equality check. Unknown version error lacks path because decoder formats just the pair. The helper recognizes accepted footer aliases only and cannot establish complete file validity.
files.limits: Complete bounded read and authored physical-line coverage. No build, test, benchmark or network execution; delegated implementations remain pending unless separately analyzed.

files.role: Public runtime facade and options for current-format file writers, plus external ColumnInfo-to-protobuf conversion. Concrete version writers own encoding, IO, initialization and completion policy.
ranges: SPDX/imports connect Arrow arrays/batches, bytes, core schema/errors, encoding column/page metadata, ObjectStore/path and prost Any. field_types is private; structural is crate-visible. ExpectedTypes is reexported pub(crate), FieldTypeMismatch publicly; public declarations inside the private field_types module are not all external API.

PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT=64 bytes and ENV_LANCE_FILE_WRITER_MAX_PAGE_BYTES exact string are crate-visible constants. This file declares but does not enforce alignment or read the environment. Public FileWriteSummary derives Debug/Clone/Copy/PartialEq/Eq, with public u64 num_rows and size_bytes; construction does not validate either.

Public Debug/Clone/Default FileWriterOptions contains optional u64 data_cache_bytes,max_page_bytes and optional bool keep_original_array. Derived Default leaves all None. Docs say runtime buffering/execution only, budget divided across columns and default8MiB per column; concrete default resolution is outside this file. Docs caution retained Arrow C-interface child arrays can pin whole batches when keeping originals.

Crate-visible validate rejects only max_page_bytes=Some(0) as InvalidInput with exact greater-than-zero message. None or positive pass; data_cache_bytes=0 and either keep_original_array state are not rejected here. No environment parsing or mutual option constraints.

Public FileWriter is an exhaustive enum holding Box of each exact V2_0,V2_1,V2_2,V2_3 Writer. No V1, trait-object variant, default or derives. Runtime methods forward to their matching version without common format policy.

Private column_info_to_metadata walks page_infos in order. Both PageEncoding::Legacy and ::Structural are prost Any-wrapped then serialized to bytes, stored in DirectEncoding; unzip copied (offset,size) pairs, preserve num_rows and priority. Collect all pages fallibly; any Any creation error aborts conversion before writer mutation by its caller. No byte fetching or range validation.

Unzip column-level buffer descriptors and serialize column.encoding as prost Any bytes in DirectEncoding; assemble ColumnMetadata with page vector. ColumnInfo.index is not a protobuf field here, so external column slice order supplies ordering. No consistency, type-url compatibility or row-count check is added in this converter.

Four From<versions::v2_x::Writer> implementations allocate one Box and construct exactly the corresponding FileWriter variant. They consume initialized/lazy concrete writer unchanged, without validation or IO.

with_page_metadata_spill consumes self, unboxes the active writer, calls its consuming builder with shared ObjectStore and owned path, then boxes that same variant again. It adds no validation or writes itself. V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 use the separately analyzed shared structural spill path; V2_0 has a separately analyzed spill implementation: whole-column length-delimited page replay replaces in-memory pages, late setup does not migrate prior pages, and the caller owns sidecar deletion. This facade itself specifies neither threshold nor sidecar cleanup.

write_batches iterates borrowed RecordBatch references and awaits self.write_batch for each sequentially. First error stops later iterations; earlier writer effects are not rolled back. Empty iterator returns Ok. The facade does not collect batches or guarantee each awaited concrete call has flushed buffered bytes.

write_batch and write_column forward asynchronously to the same enum variant, propagating Result. Column index is usize and ArrayRef is moved. No shared type/nullability/row-count/index validation is performed by these dispatch methods; concrete implementations own it.

write_external_buffer forwards borrowed bytes and returns delegated (u64,u64), documented as externally described page/column data. Alignment and tuple semantics beyond concrete writer behavior are not checked here. add_schema_metadata converts key/value Into<String> exactly once then delegates; it returns no Result and does not locally merge a map.

initialize_with_external_columns eagerly converts every Arc<ColumnInfo> to owned protobuf metadata before matching the writer. Conversion failure returns without calling any concrete initializer. Success moves schema/metadata/rows_written to the exact initializer then returns Ok; that call is not fallible in this facade. No local schema-versus-column count, current writer state or metadata-version validation. Partial conversion allocations drop on error.

add_global_buffer moves Bytes to the concrete async writer and propagates u32 index; one-based indexing is a documented contract, not computed here. finish borrows mutably and delegates Result<FileWriteSummary>, documented to close object writer. Repeated finish, flush ordering and durability require concrete implementation analysis.

abort delegates asynchronously and returns unit, so no cleanup error can be surfaced through this facade signature. It adds no cancellation/drop handler. tell delegates asynchronously as Result<u64>, documented current object position, not total buffered data or guaranteed final size.

field_id_to_column_indices borrows the exact writer mapping &[(u32,u32)] without copy or validation. Closing impl is followed by cfg(test),path=writer_tests.rs private module; this facade itself has no inline test bodies. The separate test file remains pending.
files.limits: All294 lines read. All four V2 concrete writer lifecycles, local completion/abort behavior and external metadata handling are covered by the structural-writer and V2_0 compatibility supplements. Underlying object-store completion/cleanup and writer_tests.rs remain pending. Public FieldTypeMismatch and private shared checker have separate coverage. No tests/benchmarks/builds were run.
